rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to assess if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration tests the simplest multimodal setup (concat fusion, single profile) with PCA and ResNet50 encoders, isolating the effect of modal fusion. It directly addresses the core hypothesis of multimodal benefits while keeping complexity minimal.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieved 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests weighted fusion instead of concat to isolate the impact of fusion strategy. Since fusion is a critical design choice in multimodal models, testing this variation directly addresses uncertainty about its effectiveness. It balances exploitation (building on the multimodal approach) and exploration (testing a key hyperparameter).

The existing evidence shows multimodal models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~52.6% accuracy. This experiment tests whether a simpler rna_only model with the same pca_n2000 encoder can match or exceed this baseline, isolating the impact of multimodal fusion. It balances exploration (testing a different model setting) with exploitation (using proven RNA encoder settings).

The existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models (config_016: 0.526 accuracy) outperform rna_only models. This experiment tests multiprofile (vs singleprofile) in multimodal settings, isolating the impact of profile setting. It uses the same pca_n2000 and resnet50 encoders as top-performing configs but changes profile setting, a key design choice with uncertain optimal value. This balances exploration of multiprofile (potentially higher performance) with reuse of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with pca_n2000 and resnet50 (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other settings identical (avgpool aggregation, concat fusion). This isolates the impact of the image encoder on performance, a critical design choice with high potential to improve accuracy further.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_024) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6287). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping aggregation as avgpool) can further improve performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. This is a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration and prioritizes exploitation of the promising multimodal multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.635). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation while retaining the high-performing imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method on accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (config_025: 0.6352). This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of RNA representation. It directly compares a promising RNA encoder (scvi_n200) against the current best (pca_n2000) in the top-performing configuration, which is critical for identifying optimal design choices with limited budget.

The existing evidence shows that config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with transformer aggregation instead of avgpool, isolating the effect of aggregation method. Since transformer aggregation may capture more complex patterns, this comparison clarifies whether it outperforms avgpool, maximizing exploitation of the current top-performing setup with one final experiment.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l encoders (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could isolate the impact of the RNA encoder and aggregation method. It balances exploitation of high-performing components with exploration of potential improvements, leveraging the last budget to test a promising variant.
